plan.curriculum: Mathematics 2.0, Years 5 and 6, Number (fractions, percentages), Measurement, Space, Statistics and Probability: whole-year revision of the questions on tomorrow's Grade 5 and Grade 6 General Maths tests
plan.shape: consolidation: one slide per test question type, attempted first on boards, then the method modelled on the reveal; one short I Do on related denominators, the step most likely to need reteaching
plan.criticalFeature: find what one step, one piece or one part is worth before you answer: the scale step, the same size fraction pieces, the share of the spinner
decisionPoints: the launch: which topic each student feels least sure about
the fractions hinge after the I Do
plan.anchor: Read it. Work it. Check it.
plan.catchUp: Missed Session 6? Nothing here depends on it. Anyone who wrote 6 buses on its exit ticket gets two minutes on remainders (one more bus for the leftovers) during Your turn

manipulatives: Paper strips for folding fractions (for the HELP moves)
studentTools: Printed Revision Worksheet for everyone; Extension and Supported Worksheet as needed
routineIcons: Write it, chin it, show me
boardSetup: Write the anchor on the board: Read it. Work it. Check it.

resources.label: Revision Worksheet
resources.description: Your turn. Fractions, percentages, measurement, space and chance question types again, with new numbers.
resources.title: Fractions, Measurement and Data Revision
resources.subtitle: Read it. Work it. Check it.

items.prompt: Solve. Rename to the same size pieces first.
A class raised $240. 50% bought books and 25% bought games. The rest went to charity. How much went to charity?

example.prompt: Find the perimeter of a 7 cm by 4 cm rectangle.

items.prompt: A playground is 15 m long and 8 m wide.
Tom wrote the coordinates of point T. Find his mistake and fix it.
work: T is 1 along and 4 up, so T is (4, 1).
items.answer: T is (1, 4). Along comes first, then up.

items.prompt: What is 4:25 pm in 24-hour time?
items.explain: pm adds 12 to the hours: 4 + 12 = 16, so 16:25.

items.prompt: Measure the angle.

example.prompt: A die is numbered 1 to 6. What is the chance of rolling a number less than 3?

items.prompt: Scores: 2, 5, 3, 5, 1, 5, 2, 4. What is the mode?
Spinner A has 4 equal parts and 1 is blue. Which spinner has the same chance of blue?
items.explain: 1 in 4 is the same as 2 in 8. 2 in 4 is a half, and 1 in 8 is smaller.

items.prompt: Design a spinner with 3 possible outcomes where red is the most likely. Explain why red is most likely.
items.answer: Example: 6 parts, 3 red, 2 blue, 1 green. Red has the most parts, so it has the biggest chance (3 in 6).

resources.label: Extension
resources.description: Early finisher option. Fraction and percent puzzles, measurement challenges and spinner design, with worked examples.
resources.title: Extension: Maths Investigator
resources.subtitle: Use what you know in new ways.

sections.title: Fraction and percent puzzles
sections.intro: Percent means out of 100. 25% is one quarter, 50% is one half, 75% is three quarters.

items.prompt: A shop takes 25% off a $64 game. What is the new price?
Which is the odd one out?
Find two fractions with different denominators that add to 3/4. Find another pair.
items.answer: 1/2 + 1/4, or 1/2 + 2/8, or 1/4 + 4/8 (any correct pair with different denominators).

sections.title: Measurement challenges
sections.intro: Perimeter is the distance around. Area is the space inside.

example.prompt: A square has a perimeter of 24 cm. What is its area?
steps: A square has 4 equal sides: 24 divided by 4 is 6 cm.

items.prompt: Two rectangles both have a perimeter of 20 cm. One is 6 cm by 4 cm. Find another one, then say which has the bigger area.
items.answer: Any rectangle whose length and width add to 10, e.g. 7 cm by 3 cm (area 21, smaller than 24) or 5 cm by 5 cm (area 25, bigger).

items.prompt: A movie starts at 6:45 pm and lasts 1 hour and 50 minutes. When does it finish, in 24-hour time?

sections.title: Chance and data challenges
sections.intro: The same chance means the same fraction of the spinner, not the same number of parts.

example.prompt: Use 8 equal parts to make blue a 1 in 4 chance.
steps: 1 in 4 is the same as 2 in 8.

items.prompt: A spinner has 12 equal parts. How many must be red for a 1 in 3 chance of red?
Write five scores under 10 that have a mode of 7. Can you make the mode 7 using only two 7s?
items.answer: Example: 7, 7, 2, 5, 9. Yes, two 7s works if every other score appears only once.

resources.label: Supported Worksheet
resources.description: For students who need more guidance: smaller numbers, models drawn and a hint on every question.
resources.title: Fractions, Measurement and Data: Step by Step
resources.subtitle: Take it one step at a time.

steps: The pieces are the same size: quarters.

items.prompt: Circle the one that is the same as 50%.

example.prompt: Find the perimeter of a 5 cm by 2 cm rectangle.

items.prompt: Find the perimeter of a 6 cm by 3 cm rectangle.
Find the area of a 4 cm by 5 cm rectangle.
Write 3:00 pm in 24-hour time.
items.hint: For pm, add 12 to the hours: 3 + 12.

example.prompt: A spinner has parts red, red, blue. How many possible outcomes?
steps: List each colour once: red, blue.

items.prompt: What are the coordinates of point K?
items.hint: Go along the bottom first, then up.

items.prompt: A spinner has 4 equal parts: red, red, blue, green. How many possible outcomes?

slides.notes: Session 7 this week: test revision part 2 of 2, fractions, measurement, space, data and chance.
Before you start: boards, markers and a protractor for everyone, scrap paper, and print the Revision Worksheet for all, plus a few Extension and Supported copies.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning to show what we know about fractions, measurement, space and data, ready for the test.
successCriteria: I can read a scale, a grid or a graph to find a value.
I can solve fraction, percentage and measurement problems and check they make sense.
I can explain why an answer is right using the picture or the numbers.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: Today we cover the rest of tomorrow's test:
fractions, measuring, shapes and grids, graphs and chance.
SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three... one, two, three.
SAY: Every question is a practice twin of a test question,
so you'll know exactly what each one wants.
notes.prep: SC1 reading scales, grids and graphs is reachable for all; SC2 fraction, percent and measurement problems is the core and the exit evidence; SC3 explaining is the stretch.

slides.title: Read it. Work it. Check it.

visual.banner: Tomorrow's test: show what you know

notes.answer: open - each student names one topic
beats: POINT to the three steps.
SAY: Same three steps as last session: read it, work it, check it.
Today there's one new reminder: what is one step worth?
POINT to the Today strip.
SAY: These are today's topics. Some will feel easy and some won't.
ASK: Which topic do you feel least sure about? Write just that word.
10 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: one topic word
SCAN boards and tally the topics.
80%+ -> topics spread out: keep the pace, skip the OPTIONAL slides.
Less -> most chose one topic: slow down on that block, re-ask at its end.
notes.prep: 60 to 90 seconds. About 70 seconds per question slide. Optional if short of time: 75 percent, best unit, which point is at (3, 6), outcomes, categories.

slides.title: Write the fraction at each dot

beats: SAY: Count the gaps between 0 and 1 first.
That tells you the size of each step.
ASK: What fraction is at each dot, from left to right?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
SCAN boards for ninths.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call: How did you know it was eighths?
Less -> number every tick together in eighths, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: There are 8 gaps, so each step is one eighth.
2 eighths is the same as one quarter. Tick it or fix it.
trap: counting the ticks, not the gaps, and getting ninths.
Fix: a finger in each gap to count, then they relabel.
notes.stretch: Where would 5/8 go? And 7/8?
notes.help: Label every tick in eighths first.
notes.prep: Twin of Grade 5 Q4: same skill and format, new numbers.

beats: SAY: Compare each fraction with one half.
That sorts most of them straight away.
ASK: Can you write these fractions in order, smallest to largest?
40 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
SCAN boards for 2/3 placed first.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call: Why is 2/8 the smallest?
Less -> line each up against one half on a wall, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 2/8 is a quarter, 4/10 is just under a half, 5/10 is a half,
and 2/3 is more than a half. Tick it or fix it.
trap: thinking a bigger denominator means a bigger fraction.
Fix: bigger denominator, smaller pieces. They redraw two and compare.
notes.stretch: Add 3/5 to the list. Where does it go?
notes.help: A fraction wall to line each one up against one half.
notes.prep: Twin of Grade 6 Q4: same skill and format, new numbers.

beats: SAY: Percent means out of 100, so 75 percent is 75 hundredths.
ASK: Which two cards show the same amount as 75 percent?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 3/4 and 0.75
SCAN boards for 75.0.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> shade 75 squares on a hundred grid and count the quarters, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 75 hundredths is 0.75, and 3 quarters of 100 is 75.
Tick it or fix it.
trap: choosing 75.0 because it has 75 in it.
Fix: 75.0 is seventy-five wholes, so they choose again.
notes.stretch: Write 75 percent two more ways.
notes.help: A hundred grid with 75 squares shaded.
notes.prep: OPTIONAL: skip if the launch shows this is secure. Twin of Grade 5 Q6: same skill and format, new numbers.

slides.title: Same size pieces first
steps: Quarters and eighths are different sizes.

beats: MODEL with the two strips.
SAY: Let me show you how I add 3 quarters and 1 eighth.
First I check the pieces.
POINT to the quarters, then the eighths.
SAY: Quarters are bigger than eighths, so I can't add them yet.
Each quarter splits into 2 eighths, so 3 quarters is 6 eighths.
ASK: So what is 6 eighths plus 1 eighth?
10 sec. Cue: Everyone, together, on three... one, two, three.
EXPECT: 7 eighths
REVEAL after the choral answer.
SAY: It's 7/8. Only the top number changes,
because the pieces stay eighths.
trap: adding tops and bottoms to get 4/12.
Fix: ask if 4/12 is bigger than 3/4, and they redo it.
notes.stretch: Use the strips to prove 4/12 can't be right.
notes.help: Fold a paper strip into quarters, then eighths.
notes.prep: Related denominators, for Grade 6 Q5 and Q6: rename to the same size pieces, then add or take away. SC2.

slides.title: What is 2/3 + 1/6?
slides.prompt: Write the letter of the answer.

options.misconception: adds the tops and the bottoms
adds the tops without renaming thirds as sixths

beats: SAY: This one is just for you, so no talking.
ASK: What is 2 thirds plus 1 sixth? Write the letter.
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: B
SCAN every board, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call one B: Why not C?
Less -> fold a strip into thirds, then sixths, re-ask with 1/2 + 1/4.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 5/6. Two thirds is four sixths, and one more sixth is five sixths.
Anyone on A or C starts Your turn on the Supported Worksheet.
trap: choosing A, 3/9.
Fix: 3/9 is less than 2/3, so they check with strips and redo it.
notes.prep: Hinge for fractions: under 80% means the strips again before the next three slides.

beats: SAY: Same size pieces first. Fifths and tenths: which one do we change?
ASK: What is 2 fifths plus 3 tenths?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 7/10
SCAN boards for 5/15.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> each fifth is 2 tenths: shade a strip of tenths together, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 2 fifths is 4 tenths, and 4 tenths plus 3 tenths is 7 tenths.
Tick it or fix it.
trap: adding tops and bottoms: 5/15.
Fix: rename fifths as tenths first, and they add again.
notes.stretch: Is 7/10 more or less than 3/4? Prove it.
notes.help: A strip of tenths: shade the fifths first.
notes.prep: Twin of Grade 6 Q5: same skill and format, new numbers.

beats: SAY: Taking away works the same way: same size pieces first.
ASK: What is 5 sixths take away 1 third?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 3/6
ACCEPT: 1/2
SCAN boards for 4/6 or 4/3.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call: Is 3/6 the same as a half?
Less -> 1 third is 2 sixths: cross off 2 of 5 shaded sixths, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 1 third is 2 sixths, and 5 sixths take away 2 sixths is 3 sixths.
That's one half. Tick it or fix it.
trap: taking 1 from 5 without renaming: 4/6.
Fix: rename the third as sixths, and they take away again.
notes.stretch: Write another take-away with an answer of one half.
notes.help: Draw 6 boxes, shade 5, then cross off a third of the boxes.
notes.prep: Twin of Grade 6 Q6: same skill and format, new numbers.

slides.title: How much of the paddock is left?

visual.text: A farmer plants 3/10 of a paddock with wheat and 4/10 with oats. How much is left?

beats: SAY: Read it carefully: we need what's left, not what's planted.
ASK: What fraction of the paddock is left?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 3/10
SCAN boards for 7/10.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> draw 10 boxes, shade 3 then 4, count the empty ones, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 3 tenths and 4 tenths is 7 tenths planted.
The whole is 10 tenths, so 3 tenths is left. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 7/10, the part that is planted.
Fix: underline left in the question, and they take it from the whole.
notes.stretch: If the wheat took 2/5 instead, how much would be left?
notes.help: Draw a strip of 10 boxes and shade each crop.
notes.prep: Twin of Grade 5 Q5: same skill and format, new numbers.

slides.title: About how many fans?
slides.prompt: 1/4 of 320 fans bought a scarf. About how many?

options.misconception: guesses without finding a quarter
divides by 3, not 4
finds a half, not a quarter

beats: SAY: A quarter means split into 4 equal groups.
ASK: About how many fans bought a scarf? Write the letter.
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: B
SCAN boards for D.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call one B: How did you find a quarter?
Less -> halve 320, then halve again on the board, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: Half of 320 is 160, and half again is 80.
80 is between 75 and 85. Tick it or fix it.
trap: choosing D, half instead of a quarter.
Fix: halve twice for a quarter, and they choose again.
notes.stretch: Which range would 1/3 of 320 be in?
notes.help: Draw a bar for 320 split into 4 equal parts.
notes.prep: Twin of Grade 6 Q8: same skill and format, new numbers.

slides.title: How much goes to the library?

visual.text: A school fair makes $360. 60% pays for prizes and 15% pays for food. The rest goes to the library.

beats: SAY: Read it: the library gets the rest.
So first, what percent is left?
ASK: How much money goes to the library?
60 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 90 dollars
SCAN boards for 270.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call: How did you find 25 percent?
Less -> a bar of four 25 percent parts: three spent, one left. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 60 and 15 is 75 percent spent, so 25 percent is left.
A quarter of 360 is 90 dollars. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 270, the amount spent.
Fix: underline the rest, and they find 25 percent.
notes.stretch: If food cost 20 percent instead, how much is left?
notes.help: Find 10 percent of 360 first, then build 25 percent.
notes.prep: Twin of Grade 6 Q9: same skill and format, new numbers.

slides.title: Which is the best unit?
slides.prompt: Ali wants to measure the length of an ant.

options.misconception: chooses a length unit that is far too big
mixes up length with capacity
mixes up length with mass

beats: SAY: Check two things: what are we measuring, and how big is it?
ASK: Which unit is best for the length of an ant? Write the letter.
15 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: C
SCAN boards for B.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> sort the four units under length, mass and capacity, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: Length is metres, centimetres or millimetres.
An ant is tiny, so millimetres. Tick it or fix it.
trap: choosing millilitres because it starts with milli.
Fix: millilitres measure liquid, so they choose again.
notes.stretch: Name something you'd measure in kilometres, and something in grams.
notes.help: A ruler: point to one millimetre and one centimetre.
notes.prep: OPTIONAL: skip if the launch shows this is secure. Twin of Grade 5 Q13: same skill and format, new numbers.

slides.title: What is the mass of the pumpkin?

beats: SAY: First find what each small step is worth.
ASK: What is the mass, in kilograms and grams?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 1 kg and 60 g
SCAN boards for 3 g or 600 g.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> 100 grams in 5 steps: count 20, 40, 60 around the dial, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: Each step is 20 grams, and the needle is 3 steps past 1 kilogram.
That's 1 kilogram and 60 grams. Tick it or fix it.
trap: counting each small step as 1 gram.
Fix: 5 steps make 100 grams, so they find one step and recount.
notes.stretch: How many more grams make 1.5 kg?
notes.help: Write the value beside every tick first.
notes.prep: Twin of Grade 5 Q14: same skill and format, new numbers.

slides.title: How much water is in the jug?

beats: SAY: Same skill: what is each step worth?
This time there are 4 steps in each litre.
ASK: How much water is there, in litres and millilitres?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 1 L and 750 mL
SCAN boards for 3 mL or 300 mL.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> 1000 millilitres in 4 steps: count 250, 500, 750 together, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: Each step is 250 millilitres, and it's 3 steps past 1 litre.
That's 1 litre and 750 millilitres. Tick it or fix it.
trap: reading 3 steps as 300 millilitres.
Fix: 4 steps make 1000, so one step is 250. They recount.
notes.stretch: How much more water would fill it to 2 litres?
notes.help: Label each step: 250, 500, 750.
notes.prep: Twin of Grade 5 Q15: same skill and format, new numbers.

slides.title: What is the perimeter of this card?

beats: SAY: Perimeter is the distance all the way around the outside.
ASK: What is the perimeter of the card?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 42 cm
SCAN boards for 21 or 108.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> trace all four sides, writing each length on the board, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 12 plus 9 plus 12 plus 9 is 42 centimetres.
Tick it or fix it.
trap: adding only the two labelled sides: 21.
Fix: they label all four sides, then add again.
notes.stretch: Draw a different rectangle with the same perimeter.
notes.help: Write a length on every side before adding.
notes.prep: Twin of Grade 5 Q16: same skill and format, new numbers.

slides.title: What is the area of this poster?

beats: SAY: Area is the space inside.
For a rectangle, we multiply the length by the width.
ASK: What is the area of the poster?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 2100 square centimetres
SCAN boards for 100, 200 or 210.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> 3 times 7 is 21, so 30 times 70 is 21 hundreds. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 30 times 70 is 2100 square centimetres.
Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 210, losing a zero.
Fix: 3 tens times 7 tens is 21 hundreds. They rewrite it.
notes.stretch: Find another rectangle with an area of 2100 square centimetres.
notes.help: Work out 3 times 7 first, then add the zeros.
notes.prep: Twin of Grade 5 Q17: same skill and format, new numbers.

beats: SAY: Area is length times width. We know the area and one side.
ASK: What is the length of the side with the question mark?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 70 m
SCAN boards for 2760.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> write 40 times what is 2800, then try 4 times what is 28. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 40 times 70 is 2800, so the missing side is 70 metres.
Tick it or fix it.
trap: taking 40 away from 2800.
Fix: they write 40 times what equals 2800, then solve it.
notes.stretch: What is the perimeter of this field?
notes.help: Cover the zeros: 4 times what is 28?
notes.prep: Twin of Grade 6 Q16: same skill and format, new numbers.

slides.title: What is 7:42 pm in 24-hour time?
slides.prompt: Write the letter of the answer.

options.misconception: forgets to add 12 for pm
adds 10 instead of 12
miscounts the hours past noon

beats: SAY: For pm times, add 12 to the hours. The minutes stay the same.
ASK: What is 7:42 pm in 24-hour time? Write the letter.
15 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: C
SCAN boards for A.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> count on from 12 noon to 7 pm on a timeline, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 7 plus 12 is 19, so it's 19:42. Tick it or fix it.
trap: choosing 07:42, the morning time.
Fix: ask am or pm, add 12 for pm, and they choose again.
notes.stretch: What is 23:05 in 12-hour time?
notes.help: A 24-hour strip from 0 to 24 to count along.
notes.prep: Twin of Grade 5 Q18: same skill and format, new numbers.

slides.title: Latest bus from Park St to the Beach?

notes.answer: 4:22 pm, Bus 3 in the Station to Beach table
beats: SAY: First choose the table going the right way.
ASK: What is the latest bus from Park St that gets to the Beach?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 4:22 pm
SCAN boards for 3:48 pm.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> which table's last stop is the Beach? Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: The bottom table goes to the Beach.
Its last bus from Park St is 4:22 pm. Tick it or fix it.
trap: reading the top table: 3:48 pm.
Fix: find the table ending where you're going, and they reread.
notes.stretch: How long does that bus take to reach the Beach?
notes.help: Cover the wrong-way table.
notes.prep: Twin of Grade 6 Q13: same skill and format, new numbers.

slides.title: When does the flight land?
slides.prompt: A flight leaves at 21:15 and takes 10 hours and 50 minutes.

options.misconception: forgets the extra hour hiding in 65 minutes
does not start again from 00:00 after midnight
adds 11 hours instead of 10

beats: SAY: Count on to midnight first, then add the rest.
After midnight, the clock starts again from zero.
ASK: What time does the flight land? Write the letter.
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: B
SCAN boards for A or C.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call one B: How did you get past midnight?
Less -> timeline: 21:15 to midnight is 2 h 45, then 8 h 05 more. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 21:15 to midnight is 2 hours 45.
Then 8 hours 5 more is 08:05. Tick it or fix it.
trap: adding the minutes and writing 65 minutes.
Fix: 65 minutes is 1 hour 5, and they redo it.
notes.stretch: What time would it land if the flight took 12 hours?
notes.help: A 24-hour timeline from 21:00 to 09:00.
notes.prep: Twin of Grade 6 Q14: same skill and format, new numbers.

beats: SAY: 1000 grams make 1 kilogram, so we divide by 1000.
The digits move 3 places.
ASK: How many kilograms is 4625 grams?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 4.625 kg
SCAN boards for 46.25 or 462.5.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> place value chart: 4 whole kilograms, then 625 thousandths. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 4625 divided by 1000 is 4.625.
That's 4 kilograms and 625 grams. Tick it or fix it.
trap: moving the digits only one or two places.
Fix: 1000 has 3 zeros, so 3 places. They rewrite it.
notes.stretch: Write 850 grams in kilograms.
notes.help: A place value chart with the kilograms and the point marked.
notes.prep: Twin of Grade 6 Q15: same skill and format, new numbers.

slides.title: What is the size of this angle?

beats: SAY: Find the 0 on the arm that lies flat, and count up from there.
ASK: What is the size of this angle?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 145
SCAN boards for 35.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call: Why can't it be 35?
Less -> name it first: obtuse, so over 90. Count up from the 0 together, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 145 degrees. It's obtuse, so more than 90 makes sense.
Tick it or fix it.
trap: reading 35 on the other scale.
Fix: finger on the 0 under the flat arm, and they read again.
notes.stretch: What is the angle on the other side of the line?
notes.help: Colour the row of numbers that starts at 0 on the flat arm.
notes.prep: Twin of Grade 5 Q19: same skill and format, new numbers.

beats: SAY: The square corner tells us the whole angle is 90 degrees.
ASK: What is the size of the missing angle?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 34
SCAN boards for 124 or 44.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> count up from 56 to 90: 4 to 60, then 30 more. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 90 take away 56 is 34 degrees.
Tick it or fix it.
trap: taking 56 from 180.
Fix: point to the square corner, 90 degrees, and they redo it.
notes.stretch: What if the angles were on a straight line instead?
notes.help: Count up from 56 to 90 on a number line.
notes.prep: Twin of Grade 6 Q17: same skill and format, new numbers.

slides.title: What number is at the dot?

beats: SAY: Numbers left of zero are negative. The further left, the smaller.
ASK: What number is at the dot?
15 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: -6
SCAN boards for -4 or 6.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> count back from 0 one tick at a time together, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 6 steps left of zero, so it's negative 6.
Tick it or fix it.
trap: counting from -5 the wrong way and writing -4.
Fix: count left from 0, one tick at a time, and they rewrite it.
notes.stretch: Which is bigger, negative 6 or negative 2? How do you know?
notes.help: Label every tick from -10 to 0 first.
notes.prep: Twin of Grade 6 Q1: same skill and format, new numbers.

slides.title: What are the coordinates of P?

beats: SAY: Along first, then up or down. x first, then y.
ASK: What are the coordinates of P?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: (2, -4)
SCAN boards for (-4, 2).
80%+ -> reveal, cold call: Why is the y negative?
Less -> trace from the middle: along 2, down 4, saying each move. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: Along 2 to the right, then down 4. So it's 2, negative 4.
Tick it or fix it.
trap: swapping the order: (-4, 2).
Fix: say along first, then up or down, and they rewrite it.
notes.stretch: Where would (-2, 4) be? Point to it.
notes.help: Put a finger on the middle and move along first.
notes.prep: Twin of Grade 6 Q2: same skill and format, new numbers.

beats: SAY: Same rule: along the bottom first, then up.
ASK: Which point is at 3, 6?
15 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: B
SCAN boards for A.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> trace along 3, then up 6, with a finger together, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: Along 3, up 6 is B. A is at 6, 3, the other way round.
Tick it or fix it.
trap: choosing A, at (6, 3).
Fix: say along first, then up, and they find it again.
notes.stretch: Write the coordinates of C and D.
notes.help: Run a finger along the bottom first, then up.
notes.prep: OPTIONAL: skip if the launch shows this is secure. Twin of Grade 5 Q21: same skill and format, new numbers.

slides.title: Which 3D object does this net make?

beats: SAY: Count the faces and name their shapes. That tells you the object.
ASK: Which 3D object does this net fold into?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: square pyramid
SCAN boards for triangular prism.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> fold the triangles up with your hands in the air together, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: One square base and four triangles that meet at a point.
That's a square pyramid. Tick it or fix it.
trap: calling it a triangular prism because of the triangles.
Fix: a prism has rectangles too. They count the faces again.
notes.stretch: Sketch a different net for the same pyramid.
notes.help: A paper copy of the net to cut out and fold.
notes.prep: Twin of Grade 5 Q20: same skill and format, new numbers.

beats: SAY: There are three moves: slide, flip or turn.
Look at which way the shape faces.
ASK: Was the triangle translated, reflected or rotated?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: reflected
SCAN boards for translated.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call: How can you tell it isn't a slide?
Less -> trace the triangle and flip the tracing over the line, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It faces the other way, like a mirror image across the line.
That's a reflection. Tick it or fix it.
trap: calling it a translation because it moved sideways.
Fix: check which way it faces, and they rename the move.
notes.stretch: Draw where the first triangle lands after a translation 5 to the right.
notes.help: Tracing paper to test each move.
notes.prep: Twin of Grade 5 Q22: same skill and format, new numbers.

slides.title: Slice this prism like a loaf of bread

beats: POINT to the dashed slice.
SAY: A prism is the same all the way through, like a loaf of bread.
SAY: The dashed line shows one slice, cut parallel to the end.
Picture lifting that slice out.
ASK: Turn to your partner: what will the slice look like?
10 sec. Cue: Partner A first. You have 10 seconds. Go.
EXPECT: the same shape as the end
notes.prep: Twin of Grade 6 Q18: the picture comes first, then the choice on the next slide.
notes.answer: the same shape as the end, a pentagon

slides.title: What shape is the slice?
slides.prompt: The prism on the last slide is sliced along the dashed line.

options.misconception: pictures a side face, not the slice
mixes up a prism with a pyramid

notes.answer: B - a pentagon, the same shape as the end
beats: SAY: Now choose the shape of the slice you pictured.
ASK: What shape is the slice? Write the letter.
15 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: B
SCAN boards for A.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> stack paper pentagons into a prism and lift one off. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: Each slice is a pentagon, the same as the end face.
Tick it or fix it.
trap: choosing the rectangle, a side face.
Fix: they trace the end face, then choose again.
notes.stretch: What shape is a slice of a triangular prism? A cylinder?
notes.help: A real box to look at end-on.
notes.prep: Twin of Grade 6 Q18: same skill and format, new numbers.

slides.title: How does the shape move each time?

beats: SAY: Check each move: which way does the shape face?
ASK: How does the shape move from 1 to 2, and from 2 to 3?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: reflection, then translation
SCAN boards for rotation.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call: How do you know 2 to 3 is a slide?
Less -> trace shape 1, flip the tracing onto 2, slide it to 3. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: From 1 to 2 it faces the other way, so it's a reflection.
From 2 to 3 it faces the same way, so it's a translation.
trap: calling every move a translation.
Fix: check which way each faces, and they rename the moves.
notes.stretch: Draw shape 4 so 3 to 4 is a reflection.
notes.help: Tracing paper.
notes.prep: Twin of Grade 6 Q19: same skill and format, new numbers.

beats: SAY: Negative x means go left. Negative y means go down.
ASK: Which point is at negative 3, negative 5?
15 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: B
SCAN boards for A or C.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> from the middle go left 3, then down 5, together. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: Left 3, then down 5, lands on B.
A has the numbers swapped. Tick it or fix it.
trap: going right 3 instead of left.
Fix: negative x is left, and they find it again.
notes.stretch: Write the coordinates of A and C.
notes.help: Arrows on the board: left is negative x, down is negative y.
notes.prep: Twin of Grade 6 Q20: same skill and format, new numbers.

slides.title: Which categories are best?
slides.prompt: A survey asks: How do you travel to school?

options.misconception: chooses categories that do not answer the question
uses number ranges for a question that is not about numbers
answers how often, not how

beats: SAY: Good categories match the question exactly.
ASK: Which categories are best for this survey? Write the letter.
15 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: C
SCAN boards for D.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> answer the question aloud using each set, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: The question asks how you travel,
so the answers are ways to travel. Tick it or fix it.
trap: choosing D, never to always.
Fix: that answers how often. They reread the question and choose again.
notes.stretch: Write a survey question where D would be the best categories.
notes.help: Read the question, then say your own answer out loud.
notes.prep: OPTIONAL: skip if the launch shows this is secure. Twin of Grade 5 Q23: same skill and format, new numbers.

slides.title: Which number came up most often?

visual.text: A spinner numbered 1 to 5 was spun 20 times: 3, 1, 4, 4, 2, 5, 3, 4, 1, 2, 4, 3, 5, 4, 2, 1, 3, 4, 2, 5

beats: SAY: The number that comes up most often is called the mode.
ASK: Which number came up most often?
45 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 4
SCAN boards for 2 or 3.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> tally together, crossing off each number as you go, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 4 came up 6 times, and 2 and 3 came up 4 times each.
Tick it or fix it.
trap: losing count and choosing 2 or 3.
Fix: cross off each number as it is tallied, and they recount.
notes.stretch: Which numbers came up least often?
notes.help: A tally table with rows 1 to 5.
notes.prep: Twin of Grade 5 Q24: same skill and format, new numbers.

options.misconception: checks only the tallest bar, so misses cat and bird swapped
reads the biggest and smallest the wrong way round

beats: SAY: Check the tallest bar first, then the shortest, then the rest.
ASK: Which graph matches the table? Write the letter.
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: B
SCAN boards for A.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> check every bar against the table, one pet at a time, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: Dog is tallest, fish is shortest, and cat is taller than bird.
That's B. Tick it or fix it.
trap: choosing A from the tallest bar alone.
Fix: check every bar, and they choose again.
notes.stretch: Sketch the graph if 4 more people got fish.
notes.help: Tick each pet off the table as you check its bar.
notes.prep: Twin of Grade 5 Q25: same skill and format, new numbers.

beats: SAY: There are two lines here.
Use the key to find Tuesday's line first.
ASK: At what time did Tuesday first reach 18 degrees?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 10 am
SCAN boards for 9 am.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call: Which line did you use, and why?
Less -> lay a ruler across at 18, stop at Tuesday's line, read down. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: Tuesday's line reaches 18 at 10 am.
Monday passes 18 between 8 and 9 am. Tick it or fix it.
trap: reading Monday's line and writing 9 am.
Fix: they check the key, then read again.
notes.stretch: How much warmer was Monday than Tuesday at 8 am?
notes.help: A ruler laid across the graph at 18.
notes.prep: Twin of Grade 5 Q26: same skill and format, new numbers.

beats: SAY: Each ride has two bars. Altogether means add both bars.
ASK: Which ride had the second-fewest riders altogether?
45 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: wave pool
SCAN boards for Diving or Slide.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call: What was the total for the slide?
Less -> total each ride's two bars in a table on the board. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: The slide had 40, the fewest.
The wave pool had 45, so it's second-fewest. Tick it or fix it.
trap: reading only the day pass bars and choosing Diving.
Fix: add both bars for each ride, and they choose again.
notes.stretch: Which two rides had the same total?
notes.help: A table: ride, day pass, season pass, total.
notes.prep: Twin of Grade 6 Q21: same skill and format, new numbers.

slides.title: What is the problem with this survey?
slides.prompt: The canteen asked 50 chess club members what new food to sell.

options.misconception: thinks a big sample is the problem

options.text: They should ask about drinks too
options.misconception: judges the topic, not who was asked

options.text: Only one club was asked, so it may be biased
Students from every class were asked
options.misconception: picks a strength, not a problem

notes.answer: C - only one club was asked, so the results may be biased
beats: SAY: A fair survey asks a mix of the people it is about.
ASK: What is the problem with this survey? Write the letter.
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: C
SCAN boards for A.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call: Who should they have asked?
Less -> ask: would the whole school answer like the chess club? Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: Only chess club members were asked,
so the answers may not match the whole school. Tick it or fix it.
trap: choosing A, thinking more people makes it worse.
Fix: more people is usually better. They choose again.
notes.stretch: Rewrite the survey plan so it is fair.
notes.help: Picture the whole school, then just the chess club.
notes.prep: Twin of Grade 6 Q22: same skill and format, new numbers.

beats: SAY: An outcome is a result that can happen, not a section.
ASK: How many different outcomes can this spinner land on?
15 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 3
SCAN boards for 8.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> list each colour once on the board, then count the list, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It can land on red, blue or green. That's 3 outcomes,
even though there are 8 sections. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 8, the number of sections.
Fix: list each colour once, and they count again.
notes.stretch: Which colour is least likely? Why?
notes.help: Write each colour as you find it, skipping repeats.
notes.prep: OPTIONAL: skip if the launch shows this is secure. Twin of Grade 5 Q27: same skill and format, new numbers.

slides.title: What is the chance?
slides.prompt: A 10-sided die is numbered 1 to 10. Chance of rolling more than 7?

options.misconception: counts only one number
counts 7 itself as more than 7
uses the 7 from the question

beats: SAY: List the numbers that work, then count them out of 10.
ASK: What is the chance of rolling more than 7? Write the letter.
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: B
SCAN boards for C.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call: Which numbers did you count?
Less -> write 1 to 10, circle the ones more than 7, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: More than 7 means 8, 9 and 10. That's 3 in 10.
Tick it or fix it.
trap: counting 7 as more than 7.
Fix: more than 7 starts at 8, so they count again.
notes.stretch: What is the chance of rolling an odd number?
notes.help: Write 1 to 10 and circle each number that works.
notes.prep: Twin of Grade 5 Q28: same skill and format, new numbers.

slides.title: Same chance of red?
slides.prompt: Which spinner gives red the same chance as 2 red parts out of 6?

options.misconception: matches the number of red parts, not the share
matches the number of parts, not the red share
keeps 2 red parts but adds more parts

notes.answer: B - 1 in 3, the same as 2 in 6
beats: SAY: Same chance means the same fraction of the spinner.
ASK: Which spinner gives red the same chance? Write the letter.
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: B
SCAN boards for A or D.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call one B: Prove it's the same.
Less -> write each as a fraction of red parts, then simplify. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 2 out of 6 is the same as 1 out of 3, so B.
Tick it or fix it.
trap: choosing a spinner with 2 red parts.
Fix: write each as a fraction, and they compare again.
notes.stretch: Draw a 9-part spinner with the same chance of red.
notes.help: Write a fraction under each spinner: red parts over all parts.
notes.prep: Twin of Grade 5 Q29: same skill and format, new numbers.

slides.title: Which three show a certain event?

beats: SAY: Certain means it will definitely happen.
On a chance scale from 0 to 1, that's 1.
ASK: Which three cards show a certain event?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
SCAN boards for 0 or 0.5.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> draw a 0 to 1 chance line: impossible, even chance, certain. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 1 whole, 4 out of 4 and 100 percent all mean certain.
Tick it or fix it.
trap: choosing 0.5, even chance.
Fix: they place it on the chance line, then choose again.
notes.stretch: Write three ways to show an impossible event.
notes.help: A chance line from 0 to 1 with words underneath.
notes.prep: Twin of Grade 6 Q23: same skill and format, new numbers.

notes.answer: 10 times: red is 2 out of 3, and 2/3 of 15 is 10
beats: SAY: First find the chance of red. Then take that fraction of the spins.
ASK: In 15 spins, how many times would you expect red?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 10
SCAN boards for 2 or 5.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call: Would it be exactly 10 every time?
Less -> share 15 spins into 3 equal groups of 5: red gets 2 groups. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: A third of 15 is 5, so two thirds is 10.
Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 2, the number of red parts.
Fix: they find 2 thirds of 15, then rewrite it.
notes.stretch: How many yellows would you expect in 30 spins?
notes.help: 15 counters shared into 3 groups.
notes.prep: Twin of Grade 6 Q24: same skill and format, new numbers.

slides.title: Which results are most likely?
slides.prompt: Expected in 24 spins: red 12, blue 8, green 4.

options.misconception: swaps which colour is most likely
thinks every colour comes up equally
ignores the expected results

notes.answer: B - close to the expected results, but not exact
beats: SAY: Real results are usually close to the expected results, but rarely exact.
ASK: Which table is most likely the real results? Write the letter.
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: B
SCAN boards for C.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call: Why not exactly 12, 8 and 4?
Less -> compare each table with the expected numbers, colour by colour. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: B is close to 12, 8 and 4, in the same order.
Tick it or fix it.
trap: choosing C because every colour can happen.
Fix: they compare each table with expected, then choose again.
notes.stretch: Draw a spinner that would give these expected results.
notes.help: Circle the biggest number in each table.
notes.prep: Twin of Grade 6 Q25: same skill and format, new numbers.

slides.title: Show what you know
questions: Sam ate 1/4 of a pizza and Mia ate 3/8. How much of the pizza is left?

beats: SAY: Last one, and it's just for you.
Read it, work it, check it.
ASK: How much of the pizza is left?
60 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 3/8
RECORD who writes 5/8, 4/12 or 4/8.
Give them two minutes on same size pieces before the test.
trap: writing 5/8, the part eaten.
Fix: none now. Record the name for a quick catch-up before the test.

5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
